paragraphs: Rav Yehudah bar Chaviva. Hyman cites Berakhot 41a.
Rav Yehudah was preparing for his son’s wedding at the house of Rav Yehudah bar Chaviva.

notes.text: The idiom is read as arranging his son’s marriage. Bounded checks at the cited41a, nearby41b and candidate43a did not establish the named passage; the exact source locator remains open.

The later saved named Davidson Berakhot 42a paragraph contains the exact Yehudah/son/Chaviva-house wording, supplying a match alongside source 41a despite the earlier failed lookups. The marriage-arrangement idiom is retained without inventing a named daughter or new family identity. The digital location does not establish a printer or transcription error in Hyman’s locator.

Hyman prints Berakhot 41a (מא.). The passage appears in the consulted Berakhot 42a, where wedding preparations at Rav Yehudah bar Chaviva’s house lead into a discussion about a blessing over bread. The host and the father arranging the wedding are named separately in the account.
